[[File:Solva1927 Trento2017 comparison.jpg|thumb|Francesca Vidotto pictured in a 2017 recreation of 1927 Solvay Conference. Third row, fourth from the left.]]
'''Francesca Vidotto''' (born November 22, 1980) is an Italian [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]].

==Biography==
She earned her [[Undergraduate degree|UG]]/[[Master of Arts|MA]] in [[theoretical physics]] at the [[University of Padova]] and the [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] as double-degree at the [[University of Pavia]] and the [[Aix-Marseille Université]]. Afterwards, she was a [[postdoctoral researcher|postdoc researcher]] at the universities of [[university of Grenoble|Grenoble]], [[university of Nijmegen|Nijmegen]] and [[university of Bilbao|Bilbao]].<ref>[https://inspirehep.net/authors/1071151 Francesca Vidotto] on ''inspirehep.net''</ref> 
From 2019 to 2025, she was Assistant Professor of [[Physics]] & [[Astronomy]] and [[Philosophy]] at the [[University of Western Ontario]], where she hold a [[Canada Research Chair]] in [[Foundations of Physics]]. She was also a core member and associate director of [https://www.rotman.uwo.ca/portfolio-items/vidotto/ Western's Rotman Institute of Philosophy].<ref>[https://www.uwo.ca/philosophy/people/vidotto.html Francesca Vidotto Resumé]. Since 2025, she is permanent senior researchers of the [[Spanish National Research Council]] in the center for the Structure of Matter in Madrid.</ref>

Her research explores the [[quantum]] aspects of the [[gravitational field]], in the framework of [[Loop Quantum Gravity]]. Her work covers topics from the cosmological and astrophysical applications of [[quantum gravity]] to the reflections on the nature of [[space-time]] and the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]]. She is best known for two research directions: [[Spin foam]] [[Cosmology]], and [[Planck star]]s, with special emphasis on [[white hole]]s and [[black hole|black hole remnants]]. Her main research interests have been cosmology, the quantum effect of [[Black hole|black holes]], and the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Francesca Vidotto, Assistant Professor |url=https://physics.uwo.ca/people/faculty_web_pages/vidotto.html |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=www.physics.uwo.ca |language=en}}</ref>

Vidotto won the first prize  (shared with [[Amanda Gefter]]) in the 2023 FQXi contest "How could science be different?" for her essay [https://s3.amazonaws.com/fqxi.data/data/essay-contest-files/16/essay_id_2338.pdf "How Could Science Be Different? Ask a feminist!"]. She is an advocate for equity, inclusion and diversity in the physics field.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Deborah |title=Francesca Vidotto |url=https://www.rotman.uwo.ca/portfolio-items/vidotto/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=The Rotman Institute of Philosophy |language=en-US}}</ref> She also believes [[Philosophy of science|philosophy]] and physics go hand in hand.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halley |first=Catherine |date=2020-05-29 |title=Francesca Vidotto: The Quantum Properties of Space-Time |url=https://daily.jstor.org/francesca-vidotto-the-quantum-properties-of-space-time/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=JSTOR Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Publications==

=== Scientific book ===
* ''Covariant Loop Quantum Gravity: An elementary introduction'' (with [[Carlo Rovelli]]), Cambridge University Press, 2015.<ref>[https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/covariant-loop-quantum-gravity/2DF4474CBF7845C261FA78904270F226# Covariant Loop Quantum Gravity: An elementary introduction] on ''cambridge.org/core/books''</ref>

=== Main scientific papers ===
* ''Primordial Fluctuations from Quantum Gravity'' (with Francesco Gozzini), 2019.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02211 Primordial Fluctuations from Quantum Gravity] in ''Frontiers in Astronomy and Space Sciences 7, 118''</ref>  
* ''Quantum insights on Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter'', 2018.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.08007 Quantum insights on Primordial Black Holes as Dark Matter] in ''PoS(EDSU2018)046''</ref>
* ''Planck stars'' (with Carlo Rovelli), 2014.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.6562 Planck stars] in the ''International Journal of Modern Physics D 23 (12), 1442026	240	2014''</ref>
* ''Maximal acceleration in covariant loop gravity and singularity resolution'' (with Carlo Rovelli), 2013.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3228 Maximal acceleration in covariant loop gravity and singularity resolution] in ''Physical Review Letters, 111.091303''</ref>
* ''Towards spinfoam cosmology'' (with [[Eugenio Bianchi]] and [[Carlo Rovelli]]), 2010.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.3483 Towards spinfoam cosmology] in ''Physical Review D 82 (8), 084035''</ref>
